newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb Q1 international seed results up.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb Q1 international seed results up.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp said Monday its international seed earnings rose to $5.9 million in the fiscal first quarter from $3.0 million a year ago.
International seed revenues rose nearly 53 percent to $48.1 million from $31.5 million.

"In Argentina, we are essentially sold out of all products -- corn, sunflowers, and sorghum," Bruce Bickner, chairman, said in a statement. "Corn acreage was up more than 12 percent, and once again, we were supply-constrained.
In Mexico, sorghum products are selling well and hybrid corn volume is trending higher, he added.

Earlier, DeKalb, a seed and agricultural company, reported first quarter net income of $0.12 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.01 a share. Sales rose 34 percent to $67.1 million from $50.1 million.

"First-quarter results primarily reflect seed operations in the Southern Hemisphere, as well as our swine operation," Bickner said. "The improvement over last year is due primarily to continued sales increases in Argentina, driven by demand for our new single-cross corn hybrids. In Mexico, meanwhile, our joint venture operation is generating higher earnings on higher sales volume."

DeKalb said its North American seed business reported an operating loss of $200,000 in the first quarter, compared with an operating loss of $500,000 in the prior-year period. Revenues declined 20 percent to $5.1 million from $6.4 million.

"Seed shipments of any significance do not begin until the second quarter, so the first-quarter segment results are not meaningful," Bickner said. "We are, nonetheless, very encouraged by sales activity to date. Our early cash receipts -- an excellent indicator -- are well ahead of the previous year. We believe our North American corn business is on track to report sales volume and market share gains for the fourth year in a row."
DeKalb said its Swine Breeders division earned $300,000 for the first fiscal quarter, down from earnings of $700,000 in the prior year. Revenues rose 14 percent to $13.9 million from $12.2 million.
"Despite the improved prices, our margins were hurt by high feed costs incurred during 1996, which had a negative impact on the first-quarter cost of sales," Bickner said.
